What is the equation of the parabola shown above?
feedback.worked_solution:
We know that for any upward or downward-opening parabola with its vertex at $(h,k),$ the general standard equation is given by

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k).
$$

Here, the vertex has coordinates $(h,k)=(4,0).$ Substituting these into the general standard equation, we get

$$
(x-4)^{2}=4py.
$$

We are left to find the value of $p.$ We know that the given parabola also passes through the point $(9,-5),$ so we can substitute $x=9$ and $y=-5$ into the standard equation and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-4)^{2} & =4py \\ (9-4)^{2} & =4p(-5) \\ 25 & =-20p \\ p & =-\frac{5}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-4)^{2} & =4py \\ (x-4)^{2} & =4(-\frac{5}{4})y \\ (x-4)^{2} & =-5y.\end{aligned}
$$
